interconnect_topology_options: Crossbar with one slave port and multiple master ports (each link is a TileLink agent edge in the DAG).
Hierarchical: master crossbar slave-side feeds master-side of inner crossbar which connects to multiple cache/memory slaves (Figure 2.2).
Crossbar module containing multiple independent TileLink agents — one routing agent + one configuration-access agent (Figure 2.3).
Clock-domain crossing via a TileLink-to-TileLink adapter (acts as slave in one domain and master in the other).
Power-domain crossing via a TileLink-to-TileLink adapter; both sides cannot be powered down independently while messages are inflight.
Legacy-bus bridging: TileLink-to-AXI / TileLink-to-AHB / TileLink-to-APB / TileLink-to-PCIe bridges (with timeouts on the legacy side).
interconnect_rules: Agent graph must be a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) — any cycles can lead to deadlock.
Each TileLink link consists of five physically distinct unidirectional parallel buses (channels A/B/C/D/E in TL-C; A/D-only in TL-UL/TL-UH).
All addresses are physical; every valid address must route over a single path to exactly one slave from any node in the DAG.
Crossbar's slave-side TileLink ports all connect to a single crossbar TileLink agent (since messages received on any slave port may be forwarded to any master port).
Adapter / bridge modules may contain two independent TileLink agents (one slave-side, one master-side) since messages do not directly cross — they pass through an internal queue.
When connecting a TL-C processor agent to a TL-UL device agent, the processor must refrain from advanced features, OR a TL-C-to-TL-UL adapter must be inserted.
When crossing power or clock domains a TileLink-to-TileLink adapter must be used. It is forbidden for one side of a TileLink link to power down while its opposite is powered on.

agents_and_links_definitions.operation: A change to an address range's data values, permissions or location in the memory hierarchy.
agents_and_links_definitions.agent: An active participant in the protocol that sends and receives messages in order to complete operations.
agents_and_links_definitions.channel: A one-way communication connection between a master interface and a slave interface carrying messages of homogeneous priority.
agents_and_links_definitions.message: A set of control and data values sent over a particular channel.
agents_and_links_definitions.link: The set of channels required to complete operations between two agents.
agents_and_links_definitions.master_interface: Initiates request messages; receives response messages.
agents_and_links_definitions.slave_interface: Receives request messages; sends response messages.
agents_and_links_definitions.DAG_topology_rule: A legal TileLink system must have a directed acyclic agent graph.

source_sink_id_management: source IDs uniquely identify inflight requests; they are local to a link.
Within a channel each inflight identifier must be unique; once a response is received the id may be reused.
Channel A and C requests can share source ID values across channels, since responses on D can be differentiated via d_opcode in addition to d_source.
Channel B requests need only have (b_source, b_address) uniquely inflight (relaxed because channel C responses route via c_address to a single slave).
Channel D Grant responses must provide unique d_sink IDs; channel E GrantAck uses e_sink to acknowledge.
ID widths (o, i) can vary between links. Crossbars must remap source IDs into a common namespace for downstream slaves.
address_map_recommendations: Local address map describes which regions of memory have side effects (cacheability, FIFO, executeability, privilege, QoS).
Recommend the address map not be a single global map — properties may change as messages traverse the network (e.g. an outer cache may add atomic support to inner ranges).
Recommend that address regions with Get/Put side effects be rounded to multiples of 4kB to ease TLB management.
Bursts must not under- or over-run slave address ranges; slaves must declare maximum burst support (recommended >= 4kB).
Optional FIFO domain identifier annotates regions that respond to independent requests in FIFO order.
request_response_ordering_rules: Operations may complete out-of-order; multiple operations may be inflight at any given time (Figure 5.3).
Slaves only send a response message once the effect of the operation is completed.
Response-issuing agents are responsible for ensuring a valid serialization of operations.
After ack of operation Y, slave commits to ordering and must order any later operation Z after Y.
legacy_bus_bridging_rules: TileLink-to-legacy-bus bridges must include a timeout to fit within the first forward progress rule.
If a legacy bus does not accept a request within the timeout, the bridge must discard the request and inject a TileLink error response.
If a legacy bus exceeds the response timeout, the bridge must cancel the outstanding request and inject a TileLink error response.
burst_in_progress_constraints: Bursts cannot be interleaved with beats of other messages on the same channel.
Control signals (opcode/param/size/source/address) constant across all beats of a burst.
Data addresses auto-increment per beat by the data bus width.
Final signals (c_error, d_error) may change at most once per burst and must stay HIGH once asserted.
